newsitem.title: UK: NSM to cut gearing, plans US sale, sees loss.
newsitem.headline: NSM to cut gearing, plans US sale, sees loss.

text.p: British mining group NSM Plc said on Thursday that after a detailed review of operations it had decided to reduce its gearing substantially.
It said it would achieve this, in part, by selling its U.S. operations and had appointed investment bank PaineWebber Inc. to effect the sale.

"It is expected that this sale will be at a substantial discount to net asset value," the company said in a statement, in which, it added, it expected to sell other assets, and foresaw a trading loss for the half-year ending September 30.
"The company is in discussions with its bankers regarding its immediate short-term, working capital requirements and its capital structure following the proposed disposal," the statement added.

Following the planned sale of its US business, and other disposals of non-core assets already under negotiation, the company predicted it would end up being "principally based in South Wales, supported by opencast mining operations in England and Scotland."
"The South Wales mine is scheduled to reach its forecast production tonnages by April 1997 and the quality of coal and sizes are better than originally predicted", it added.
